text:
maria: Quick sync — I ran an ablation suite this morning that varies HTTP keepalive, client pool size, TLS session reuse, and replay vs synthetic load. Hit a weird KV-cache warmup interaction that looks like a perf regression candidate. Posting numbers/configs below.

liam: TL;DR?

maria: Short: disabling keepalive (connection churn) blew up CPU and p50 for short requests. TLS handshake cost compounds when sessions aren't resumed, so p95 gets worse. Replay harness that preserves client sessions masks the issue — synthetic harness that makes fresh connections every request amplifies it. With KV-cache cold (no priming), the runtime spends extra time serializing cache misses which shifts kernel selection and hurts batching efficiency. End result: 2.4x p50 under replay-without-keepalive vs baseline where keepalive + pooled conns are used. :grimacing:

jonathan: Can you paste the exact bench config you used? want to reproduce locally.

maria: Sure — pared down k6/vegeta-ish snippets here. note the `keepalive` toggle and `pool_size` param.

```bash
# attacker config (k6 style pseudo)
SCENARIO="replay"
KEEPALIVE=true   # toggle to false for churn test
POOL_SIZE=4      # try 2,4,16
TLS_RESUME=true  # simulate session reuse toggle

# simplified request (k6/v2)
http.batch([{
  method: 'POST',
  url: 'https://api.redwood.internal/v1/generate',
  headers: { 'Connection': (KEEPALIVE ? 'keep-alive' : 'close') },
  body: JSON.stringify({ prompt: 'short prompt' })
}], POOL_SIZE)
```

ashley: This actually maps to the regression we saw in canary last week — LB config change caused downstream clients to close conns faster. Might be the same root cause. Thanks for correlating.

perf-bot: quick summary report attached: CPU +70% without keepalive, p50 240ms -> 580ms (2.4x), p95 520ms -> 1.6s, tokens/s throughput down 35% when KV-cache cold and pool_size<=4. Replay with session reuse shows only ~10% regression.

liam: So for apples-to-apples we need to control three axes in every benchmark: 1) connection behavior (keepalive, pool size, session reuse), 2) cache state (cold/warm/primed), 3) client distribution (replay preserving sessions vs synthetic fresh sessions). If any of these differ between runs you can get misleading comparisons.

maria: Agreed. Also concrete note on gRPC vs REST: gRPC multiplexes on HTTP/2 so single TCP + TLS handshake amortized across streams; REST (HTTP/1.1) often relies on many short-lived TCP conns unless keepalive/pooling is explicit. That means our HTTP harness needs explicit conn reuse to compare to gRPC.

jonathan: How did kernel selection factor in? you mentioned it changed.

maria: When KV-cache misses spike, request length distribution shifts (more recomputation, longer kv loads) which caused the runtime to pick a different kernel variant for attention/softmax optimized for longer sequences. Those kernels had worse throughput per-GPU for small batches, so batching heuristics got less efficient and tail latencies rose. We saw the timeline in perf flamegraphs: first TLS handshake, then KV miss handling, then kernel switch.

ashley: Any reproducible script we can run? I can add it to ci-perf.

maria: Yep — adding a small reproduce.sh to the perf repo, but short guidance here:

- Step A: ensure test client preserves session ids for baseline (simulate mobile/keepalive).
- Step B: run prime phase: 5k warmup requests for KV keys used in payloads, then toggles to cold by restarting runtime.
- Step C: run churned test with KEEPALIVE=false and POOL_SIZE=1.
- Step D: collect perf counters + flamegraphs, kernel selection logs.

Example client curl for manual smoke: `curl -H "Connection: keep-alive" --http1.1 -X POST https://api.redwood.internal/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'`
